draft.headline: Visual perception accounts for 73 percent of errors when top AI models fail repeated tests
draft.threads_post:
Visual perception causes 73 percent of AI errors in Google Deepmind’s latest benchmark.

Deepmind tested 18 AI models on "Humanity's First Exam." Top performers like OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra solved nearly every task family once, but stumbled when required to deliver 16 straight correct answers. Adding extra compute time did not fix the problem.

Is 100% reliability realistic for AI models, or are occasional errors inevitable?

draft.instagram_caption:
Visual perception causes 73 percent of AI errors when top models are pushed for consistency.

Google Deepmind tested 18 AI models using a benchmark called "Humanity's First Exam." Top models like OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra can solve nearly every task family at least once. But when asked to deliver 16 straight correct answers, even the leading models stumble.

Deepmind found that adding more compute time does not fix the problem, showing that extra power alone won't solve simple daily reliability.

Is 100% reliability realistic for AI models, or are occasional errors inevitable?
